title: My New Diet for Natural Hypertrophy (Vegan? Meat only?)
summary: After a channel update about copyright strikes, NH details how his diet changed over two years of self-experimentation: high carb, low fat, moderate protein, roughly 2000 kcal, no dairy or beef, and mostly fish, poultry, eggs, rice, fruit and vegetables. He argues diet is individual, that you should look at your ancestry and remove foods that don't agree with you, and that most people overeat when bulking.
claims: NH is fighting copyright claims from two Japanese companies, one allegedly blackmailing him for money; one more strike would delete the channel
NH prioritizes longevity and vitality in his diet over pure hypertrophy or strength; the two tend to go together when the diet fits your body
Diet is individual, close to spirituality; experiment on yourself by removing and adding foods instead of copying cookie-cutter bodybuilder plans
Reject broad diets and absolutes; amounts, ratios, timing and micronutrients will differ person to person
NH is a carb person: most of his calories are carbs, which improve his recovery, training capacity, muscular endurance and appearance
He eats minimal fat; a fatty homemade ramen broth left him lethargic for four hours
NH's macro split is high carbs, low fat, moderate protein
He cut animal products heavily on his nutritionist's advice based on his family history; his uncle, the only male relative to reach his 60s, did the same
Cutting animal products did not cost him strength or muscle; his health and physique improved with each one removed
He is not vegan and has no ethical objection to eating animals
He fully eliminated dairy and beef because relatives who ate them died early of diet-related disease
Soy never had negative effects on him; he eats tofu fine
Cutting milk while recomping at the same bodyweight removed his love handles, odd lumps and water retention, revealing separation and veins
Milk is a great bulker but for some ancestries the mass added is mostly bad weight
Beef and milk are not bad in themselves but may be bad for you depending on who you are; test it
Look at what your healthiest relatives eat to find out what suits you
Remove foods gradually: he dropped milk, then cow cheese, then goat cheese over two years, and pork before beef
He avoids pork as too fatty and avoids cheeseburgers and pizza
Modern diets improve more by subtraction than addition; there's no point taking an antidote while still drinking poison
His protein sources are chicken, turkey, sardines, salmon (including raw), eggs and tuna; turkey and chicken because they're low in fat
Avoid store rotisserie chicken; oven-cook poultry
Watch mercury in fish and source locally when possible
Eggs are fine; get pasture-raised eggs with deep orange yolks
Rice is his top carb; he avoids wild rice, which he digests poorly; rice can constipate in large amounts
He tolerates pasta and gluten fine; if gluten bothers you, cut it
He eats lots of lentils but no beans, and watches iron intake since too much iron is bad for him
His fats come mainly from olive oil, fish and oat milk; avoid palm oil
He drinks about one liter of oat milk a week, mixed into protein shakes
Leafy greens are his main vegetable; he eats large amounts of vegetables daily, plus mushrooms, carrots, tomatoes and peppers
Focus on micronutrients; a balanced diet removes the need for vitamin supplements, which are crutches
Drop foods you don't digest, like broccoli for him, even if they're nutritious
Carnivore and vegan diets help people mainly because they remove processed junk, not because of the food group itself
In summer he eats mostly fruit: two mangoes a day, grapefruit, dozens of cherries, citrus, berries, bananas
He could keep his physique on processed carbs, but his insulin sensitivity and health would suffer
People with low metabolisms do better snacking plus occasional big meals than eating six big meals a day
NH eats around 2000 kcal a day at 6'2" while maintaining and gaining muscle
Most people eat too much; a surplus does not automatically turn into muscle, and excess becomes fat
Bulks are weapons to be used with care
He doesn't count calories, plan meals or meal prep; meal prepping on a budget made him hate his food
Many young men develop eating disorders from YouTube and Instagram diet culture
